articleTitle: Major industrial installations extensions and commercial developments
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Installation of Electrical Equipment in Major Building Projects
abstract: The author outlines a contractor's view of the problems associated with major industrial electrical installations, many of which have been around for a number of years. The author identifies a need for tight programme control and adequate planning. A requirement for liaison with other trades and personnel involved in the project is also established.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of the electrical contractor
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Installation of Electrical Equipment in Major Building Projects
abstract: The role of the electrical contractor on a major building site is to carry out the installation and commissioning of the electrical equipment and services as specified in the contract. This work will be the culmination of the basic electrical design prepared by the consultants in conjunction with the architects. The electrical contractor will work closely not only with the consultants and the architect but also with the suppliers of electrical equipment and the electricity supply authority, as well as liaising with other contractors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Installation of Electrical Equipment in Major Building Projects
abstract: Embankment Place is a new office building that has been constructed over the existing Charing Cross railway station in London. The London Electricity Board provided a 7 MVA electricity supply at high voltage using an existing 22 kV distribution network. Six substations were necessary with a 6.6 kV switchboard and associated metering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
